children.text: bhaktebhyo bhuvanādhipatyavaradaṃ devair mahendrādibhiḥ siddhaiścāraṇaguhyakair munigaṇaiḥ proddiṣṭapādāmbujam
children.translated_text: For his devotees he grants lordship over the worlds; gods beginning with great <s>Indra</s>, siddhas, cāraṇas, guhyakas, and hosts of sages point out his lotus feet.

children.text: saṃsārabhramabhīruṇā ca manasā dhyāyanti yaṃ yoginaḥ taṃ vande śaśikhaṇḍamaṇḍitajaṭājūṭaṃ bhavaṃ dhūrjaṭim ||
children.translated_text: Yogins, with minds fearful of the wandering of saṃsāra, meditate on him. I bow to <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, whose mass of matted hair is adorned with a crescent moon.
Then, having given the purīṣa, through a desire to behold the jewel-cow,
the illustrious <s>Caṇḍeśvara</s> composed the wondrous <s>Ratnadīpikā</s>.
Among the nine jewels, according to the origins, qualities, and classes of the substances,

children.text: guṇo nirīkṣyate teṣu śodhanaṃ cātra kathyate ||
children.translated_text: their quality is examined, and here their purification is also explained.
Sages such as <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, and <s>Varāha</s>, in the ocean of jewels,
having churned it with the mountain of knowledge, brought forth the nectar of the nine jewels.
There jewels are of various kinds, divided into great jewels and subsidiary jewels.
Among them five jewels are principal, and the group of four are subsidiary jewels.
Here they are written separately, according to their value and according to their quality.

children.text: vajraṃ ca mauktikaṃ caiva māṇikyaṃ nīlameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Diamond, pearl, ruby, and also sapphire,
and emerald are to be known as the five kinds of great jewels.
I shall state the four subsidiary jewels; listen to that.

children.text: gomedaṃ puṣparāgaṃ ca vaiḍūryaṃ ca pravālakam
children.translated_text: Hessonite, yellow sapphire, cat's-eye, and coral are the subsidiary jewels.

children.text: vajraṃ ca mauktikaṃ śvetaṃ māṇikyaṃ rohitaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: Diamond and pearl are known as white, and ruby as red.

children.text: nīlaṃ nīlaṃ samākhyātaṃ marakataṃ haritaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: Sapphire is called blue, and emerald is known as green.

children.text: śvetaṃ pītaṃ ca gomedaṃ puṣparāgaṃ ca piñjaram ||
children.translated_text: Hessonite is white and yellow, and yellow sapphire is tawny.

children.text: pravālaṃ lohitaṃ proktaṃ vaiḍūryaṃ pāṇḍuraṃ harit
children.translated_text: Coral is said to be red, while cat's-eye is pale and greenish.

children.text: siṃhale ca kaliṅge ca mātaṅge ca himālaye
children.translated_text: In <s>Siṃhala</s>, in <s>Kaliṅga</s>, in <s>Mātaṅga</s>, and in the <s>Himālaya</s>,
and in <s>Pāraskara</s> and <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> are the places where diamonds originate.
The classes of diamonds are white, red, yellow, black, and so on.
They are female, male, and neuter; one should identify them by their marks.
When held in other water and filled with water, they become larger.
Those are called male which are free from lines and spots.
Those furnished with lines and spots and having six angles are regarded as female.
Those that are triangular, thin, and not long are to be known as neuter.
Among all of them the males are best; they bind mercury more powerfully.
A female diamond is for bodily purification; the neuter is counted among the impotent type.
The Brahmin type is prescribed for rasāyana, and the Kṣatriya type for destroying disease.
The Vaiśya-class one is for ailments such as tumors; the fourth type is for arresting virility.

children.text: strī tu strīṇāṃ pradātavyā klībaṃ klībe tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: A female one should be given to women, and likewise a neuter one to a neuter person.
Male diamonds, being stronger, are always fit to be used for all persons.
People who wear jewels that have been properly prepared on their own bodies
obtain sons, wives, and wealth, and there is constant festivity in their house.
They praise a high diamond, six-angled, light, and shining.
It has a very sharp edge, eight points, and is smooth with rays on every side.
It is six-angled and eight-sided, with twelve edges and rays.
Excellent, middling, and sharp are qualities arising from its form.

children.text: vidyād indradhanurdīptaṃ svacchāyā śreyam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: One should know as superior a diamond blazing like a rainbow and clear in its own luster.
Lightness when crossing water, and firmness that withstands hard blows,

children.text: cirāvasthānajaṃ śaucaṃ vajre va kā guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and purity produced by long endurance: these are the qualities in a diamond.

children.text: stasmi svaṣṭākaprabhava śaśikalāṅkāśavarṇo dvijaś cāraktadyutimatpriyaṅgukusumacchāyastathā kṣatriyaḥ
children.translated_text: In this classification, the Brahmin diamond is born from the auspicious eightfold source and has the color of the moon's mark; the Kṣatriya is reddish and lustrous, like the shade of a priyaṅgu flower.

children.text: vaiśyaḥ śvetaniśāprasūnasadṛśaḥ śītāṃśudīptirbhavet śūdraḥ kṛṣṇarucistathāpi śivasteṣāṃ caturṇāṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: The Vaiśya resembles a white night-blooming flower and has the brilliance of the moon; the Śūdra has black luster, yet all four are auspicious in their order.
Its radiance is like <s>Śakra</s>'s bow, and its brilliance equals moonstone.
It is manifest like a split sunbeam, with a clear line visible in its support.
Untimely death, snakes, fire, fears from all diseases,

children.text: tathāśubhāni naśyanti vajraṃ yasya gṛhe sthitam ||
children.translated_text: and likewise inauspicious things perish for the one in whose house a diamond is kept.

children.text: ūrdhve nivārayed vajraṃ vane siṃhāṃśca vārayet
children.translated_text: Held above, a diamond wards things off; in the forest it wards off lions.
At night a man wards off spirits by carrying it in his hand.
A diamond that is six-angled, pure, sharp-pointed, and free from all faults,

children.text: tīkṣṇadhāraṃ ca yad vajraṃ lakṣamūlyaṃ tu tadbhavet ||
children.translated_text: and that has a sharp edge, has a value of one lakh.
Water-drop marks, barley-lines, marks like those of Vaiśyas, and crow's-foot marks
are faults to be rejected, for they give various visible results.
That diamond should be put on a balance; afterward its value should be determined.

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ hitaṃ śvetaṃ pītābhaṃ bhūbhujāṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: White is beneficial for Brahmins; yellowish is beneficial for kings.

children.text: āraktābhaṃ tu vaiśyānāṃ śūdrāṇām asitaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Reddish is beneficial for Vaiśyas, and black is beneficial for Śūdras.
By eight white mustard seeds one barley grain is said to be measured.
According to its compact mass, one should determine the value of the diamond.
By the measure of a barley grain in a vessel, or, with difficulty, by a grain of rice,

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ yavamātraṃ ca kāntiḥ sarvatra dūṣyate
children.translated_text: if faultless and of barley-grain size, its brilliance is everywhere assessed.
Its value is five hundred, as is stated also in the Ratnasāra.

children.text: piṇḍaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ mūlye vajra va tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: When the mass is doubled, the value of the diamond becomes doubled likewise.
The value may become fourfold; threefold and eightfold are also recognized.
If there is a sequential increase of four, five, six, and so forth,
then its value is just doubled, as stated in the jewel science.

children.text: gurutve cādhanāmaṃ mūlyaṃ sāmānye madhyamaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: When it is heavy, the value is low; when it is ordinary, it is remembered as middling.
When light, the value is excellent; thus there are excellent, inferior, and middling grades.
One should consider the compact mass mentally, and afterward determine the value.

children.text: śvetapītaṃ ca raktābhaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ vā kuliśaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt-jewel may be white, yellow, reddish, or black.
In the order beginning with Brahmin, one should establish the distinction of class.

children.text: uttamaṃ brāhmaṇe mūlyaṃ madhyamaṃ kṣatriye śrutam ||
children.translated_text: The highest value is for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> type; the middling value is heard for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
An ordinary value applies to one of the <s>Vaiśya</s> class, and the lowest to one born as a <s>Śūdra</s>.

children.text: yanmūlyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ proktaṃ pādādhaḥ kṣatriye bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The value that is declared for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> becomes a quarter less for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
In this very order, our examiner says the same.

children.text: kṛtrimatvaṃ yadā vajre śakyate sūribhiḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: When artificiality in a diamond can somehow be detected by experts,

children.text: kṣārāmlair lepayed vajraṃ raudre caiva parikṣipet
children.translated_text: one should smear the diamond with alkaline and acidic substances and then place it in the sun.
Afterward the discoloration of the artificial kind is seen together with it.
And from excessive rubbing it is worn away; its powder goes to the state of powder.
But that which is called vāritara has the luster of a blade of <s>dūrvā</s> grass.
Where the powder has extent, that jewel is fit for a crore.
This <s>Māhendra</s> jewel should be worn, for it grants abundance of wealth and grain.
It grants sons, is purifying and worthy of worship, destroys enemies, and gives strength and nourishment.
It grants sons, is purifying and worthy of worship, destroys enemies, and gives fearlessness in battle.
It is to be placed ... the jewel of benefit and protection; the wording is corrupt.
By contact with a diamond in the belly, the embryo is dissolved, auspiciously.
Even by <s>Śūdras</s> it is to be worn; the jewel protects the neck and chest, though the text is corrupt.
From contact with the embryo in the belly, one should know that then it becomes stronger.
If one afterward wears it through ignorance, it is to be avoided.
Likewise, a diamond on the head; the wording about the diamond and thunderbolt is corrupt.
For an inferior person the excellent is equivalent, and for an excellent person the inferior likewise.
The middling one, because of fear, would act in the face of every severe danger.
Inferior people make diamonds into mere marks and make them useless.
One should test them with experts in the science, by rubbing on a touchstone and by scratching.

children.text: lauhāni yāni ratnāni sarvaratnāni yāni ca
children.translated_text: Whatever metallic jewels there are, and whatever all the jewels are,

children.text: tāni vajreṇa lekhyāni tair vajraṃ ca na likhyate ||
children.translated_text: they are to be scratched with a diamond, but a diamond is not scratched by them.
In <s>rasāyana</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> type becomes a giver of auspicious success.
The red <s>Kṣatriya</s> conquers death and removes wrinkles, gray hair, and disease.
The <s>Vaiśya</s> becomes beneficent; having a yellow body, it produces freedom from disease.

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ śūdro rujaṃ hanti vīryastambhaṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: The black <s>Śūdra</s> removes illness and also causes retention of virility.

children.text: strīpuṃnapuṃsakā ye ca lakṣaṇena tu lakṣyate
children.translated_text: Those that are female, male, and neuter are to be recognized by their characteristics.
In the previous order these are the best, pure and having the color of mercury.
They produce bodily radiance, give enjoyments, and bring many women.
The neuter ones have little potency; the female ones are lustful and devoid of strength.
A water-drop, a barley mark, a line, and, for the <s>Vaiśya</s>, a crow's-foot mark:
these five faults are stated, giving only inauspicious results.
If there is on its surface a crow's-foot shape, marked by a red speck,

children.text: saṃtānaṃ naśyate vajraṃ kṣemakāryāya na kvacit ||
children.translated_text: the diamond destroys offspring and is never for welfare-making.
If there is a dirty flaw among the lines, in the middle of the jewel,
that jewel is declared fruitless by those skilled in jewel science.

children.text: dhāgaṇī padārāya ūrdhvaṃ cāsiprahārāya chedacchedāya bindubhiḥ
children.translated_text: For striking upward, for a sword-blow, for cutting and severing, by spots; the opening words are corrupt.
A red one brings victory over elephants and horses; a yellow one brings destruction of enemies.

children.text: āyur dhānyaṃ dhanaṃ lakṣmīṃ kṛṣṇo nāmapadaṃ kṣayet
children.translated_text: A black one destroys life, grain, wealth, prosperity, and name and status.
It may be rightward or leftward, and may also go upward with cuts and divisions.
In a diamond, the wise identify four kinds of lines by their visible scratches.
Small, eight-pointed, six-angled, with sharp edges and very pure:
a diamond furnished with a crow's-foot mark surely indicates death.
One that is pierced by external substance, broken at the angle, or very round,
is not capable of producing its auspicious or inauspicious result.
Joined with a red speck, broken, or furnished with a crow's-foot mark,

children.text: vajraṃ na śasyate puṃsāṃ kṣemāya vijayāya ca
children.translated_text: a diamond is not recommended for men's welfare and victory.
An unpurified diamond causes pain in the heart and side, leprosy, and illness.
Pallor, heat, and heaviness also arise when that diamond has not been purified.
An unpurified diamond bears jaundice, pain in the side, skin disease, burning, continuation of distress,

children.text: rogādikaṃ gurutvaṃ ca dhatte vajram aśodhitam ||
children.translated_text: and disease and the like, as well as heaviness.
Born from clouds, elephants, fish, snakes, bamboo, conches, and boars,
and born from oyster shells: these are to be known as the eight kinds of pearl.
Among them, one is easily obtained, the oyster-born one, famous in the world.
Only at some time, after long periods, is a pearl-fruit seen.
The cloud-born is very white in appearance; the elephant-born is rosy and shining.

children.text: matsyaṃ śvetaṃ tu tadvacca phaṇīndre nīlabhāsvaram ||
children.translated_text: The fish-born is white in the same way, while in the lord of snakes it is blue-shining.

children.text: haricchvetaṃ tathā vaṃśe pītaśvetaṃ ca sūkare
children.translated_text: In bamboo it is greenish white, and in the boar yellowish white.
The pearl-jewel born from conch and oyster is white and unsurpassed.
That which is born from conch or oyster and arises from the milk ocean,
well-rounded, very bright, and high, is praised as a pearl-jewel.

children.text: śītalaṃ prāṇadaṃ śuklaṃ guru svacchaṃ sunirmalam
children.translated_text: Cool, life-giving, white, heavy, clear, and very pure,
with abundant brilliance and well-rounded: such a pearl is most endowed with qualities.

children.text: surañjanaṃ guru snigdhaṃ suvṛttaṃ nirmalaṃ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Beautifully colored, heavy, smooth, well-rounded, clear, and distinct:

children.text: kathyante ratnaśāstrajñair mauktikasya ca ṣaṭ guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these are said by experts in jewel science to be the six qualities of a pearl.

children.text: madhupītasitatvaṃ ca chāyā ca trividhā matā
children.translated_text: Honey-colored, yellow, and white are regarded as three kinds of shade.
They are to be known by experts in jewel science when determining the shade of a pearl.
Whiteness, well-roundedness, straightness, fineness, and good perforation,
and good luster are praised by those skilled in jewel science.
White, red, yellow, and black, in that order:
whatever value is declared for a white pearl-jewel,
for a red and the others in sequence, the jewel is less by one quarter.
Blue in shade, well-rounded, and resembling the fruit of the karkaṭī plant,
he also obtains vehicles and a wealth of jewels, preceded by elephants and horses,

children.text: prāpnotyeva sadā so'pi gṛhe yasya sthito maṇiḥ ||
children.translated_text: always indeed, in whose house that jewel is kept.
As large as a jujube fruit, brilliant, and equal to hailstones,
that is declared to be the mark of the jewel, bestowing the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
There are nine faults and five qualities, according to the divisions of shade and brilliance;
and <s>Dhaneśvara</s> has stated the eightfold valuation of the pearl.
One should reject a pearl that is pierced, rough, small, reddish, excessively long,

children.text: malinaṃ niṣprabhaṃ citraṃ bhagnaṃ ca mauktikaṁ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: dirty, without brilliance, variegated, or broken.

children.text: svacchabhāvaṃ suvṛttaṃ ca guru snigdhaṃ ca nirmalam
children.translated_text: Clear in nature, well-rounded, heavy, smooth, and spotless,
and resembling a raised drop: such a pearl-jewel is unsurpassed.
The Brahmin type should be white in shade; the Kṣatriya bears the rays of the sun.
The Vaiśya should be yellowish in shade, and the Śūdra is considered black in luster.
By eight white mustard seeds a barley grain is said to be measured,
and by four barley grains there is one guñjā; thus one should determine the price.
Well-rounded, very bright, white, and of the measure of a guñjā, it is unsurpassed;
its price is twenty-five, as stated in the jewel science.
With a price increasing one by one, and by the sequence of increase in guñjās,
the valuation of a pearl is made according to the influence of its qualities and faults.
Sixty-four guñjās are called one padyānaka,
and the excellent pearl which has that jewel-measure is worth a crore.

children.text: mānena vartate muktā tathā mūlyaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: As a pearl is measured, so its price proceeds;

children.text: hīyate ca tathā muktā yathā hīnā ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: and likewise a pearl decreases in value as it becomes deficient.

children.text: mauktike yadi sandehaḥ kṛtrimaḥ sahajo'pi vā
children.translated_text: If there is doubt about a pearl, whether it is artificial or natural,
then a test should be made by those skilled in the jewel science.
One should place it in a vessel of cow urine mixed with salt and milk,
or heat it by fire, and wrap it in a white cloth.
Taking the pearl in the hand, one should rub it with rice chaff;
the artificial one loses its pleasantness, while the natural one shines exceedingly.

children.text: mauktikaṃ tu madhuraṃ suśītalaṃ dṛṣṭidoṣaśamanaṃ viṣāpaham
children.translated_text: A pearl is sweet, very cooling, allays eye disorders, and removes poison;
it destroys the agitation of royal consumption and becomes efficacious, giving virility and nourishment.

children.text: siṃhale ca suvele ca malaye gandhamādane
children.translated_text: In <s>Siṃhala</s>, <s>Suvela</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
in the belly and marshy shore of the ocean, are the places where rubies arise.
I shall explain the fourfold division of the classes of ruby,
namely Brahmin, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra, in that order.
The jewel that is bluish-red and produced as ratna-saugandhika,
bound together by various mineral elements, is the stone called kuruvindaka.
That which arises from crystal should be pure; such are the distinctive qualities.

children.text: ratnaṃ śvetaṃ bhavedvipraḥ suraktaṃ kṣatriyaḥ śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A white jewel is the Brahmin type, while a deeply red one is known as Kṣatriya.
A red but yellowish one is Vaiśya; likewise one that is red-yellow is the outcaste type.
It may have the form of a red lotus, or brilliance equal to a red coal,
or be red like a cuckoo's eye, or resemble the eye of a sārasā crane.
It may have the appearance of the eyes of the koka and khañjana birds; its faults are like fire in brilliance.
The kuruvindaka that resembles a pomegranate or a kiṃśuka flower is Kṣatriya.
One like cinnabar or a red flower, blackish and red,
and much like the juice of hibiscus and lac, is regarded as the Vaiśya saugandhika.
Possessing very red brilliance, with a line like iron, and smooth,
and having the form of a piece of flesh, it is the outcaste type and produces evil.
Whatever the price of a padmarāga is, that price has been stated for it.
The dark kandaka is worth that price less by one quarter,
as much as the price has been declared by the learned among the Vaiśya classes.
A quarter of that price is given for one born in the Śūdra class.
They praise a light jewel; heaviness belongs to the padmarāga.
It is soft like a pearl, and may be deep blue, white, or red.
There is an upward-facing, downward-facing, side-facing, and dark jewel.
By the distinction of compactness and weight they are superior, inferior, and middling.
The jewel that is seen from afar with the luster of water and fire
should be known by those skilled in jewel science as possessing watery brilliance.
Having made it like the young sun, one should hold a mirror there.
There, according to the division of brilliance, one should determine its class and price.
According to a measure of one, two, three, four, or five white mustard seeds,
the valuation of jewels proceeds; one should determine each one's price accordingly.
And, for the jewel, its speed or force is according to its measure.
The value of a padmarāga is a hundred increased by ten.
If, in mustard-seed measure, vessel-like brilliance exists one by one,
one should state a doubled price up to twenty mustard seeds.
If any doubt arises whether it is artificial or natural,
one should rub jewel against jewel; from that a streak is damaged or destroyed.

children.text: nīlaṃ vā padmarāgaṃ vā ratnaṃ tenaiva lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: By that a blue gem or a padmarāga gem is recognized.
A diamond is tested only by a harder diamond; there is no deliberation to be made here.
A rubbed, pure ruby-born stone is not split by iron.
If it moves or flashes upward, that jewel is pure and bestows wealth.
But if it is split, flawed, or born like sugar-gravel,
soft, tree-like, or machine-marked, that jewel becomes fault-giving.
One called aṅkola-fruit or conch-shaped destroys sons and good fortune.
And one like an aśoka fruit or a fenced growth indeed causes poverty.
A jewel resembling honey brings wealth and the good fortune of sons.

children.text: aṅkadinaṃ ca yadratnaṃ yasya veśmani tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: But the jewel called aṅkadina, when it stays in a person's house,
brings reproach, poverty, anxiety, grief, and fear.
Blue sapphire is said by the wise to be fourfold according to distinction of color.
Its origin is varied in the mines, through the conjunction of fate.
It may be white-blue, yellow-blue, red-blue,
or also black-blue; these are to be understood in the order beginning with Brahmin.

children.text: siṃhale ca kaliṅge ca nīlānāmākaraṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: They know mines of blue sapphires in <s>Siṃhala</s> and <s>Kaliṅga</s>.
That born in <s>Siṃhala</s> is the best, and that born in <s>Kaliṅga</s> is middling.
The faults of blue sapphire are sixfold, and its qualities likewise are fivefold.
The śūdraka type, a pinkish shade, a rough appearance, and perforation,
a value of sixteen is stated; through qualities of shade and excellence it may be otherwise.
Soft-stone, silvery appearance, and mahānīla are also blemishes.
In the śūdraka there is poverty; in the pinkish one there is conflict with enemies.
By its shade there is loss of beauty, and slander arises from the three.
Exile from one's country and poverty are the great result of roughness.
A triangular stone gives fear of enemies; one should declare a variegated black one to be faulty.
Thus the many kinds of faults in a jewel are to be rejected by the wise.
I shall tell their qualities, as they were seen by the ancients.
Heavy, smooth, rich in color, and charming those who stand nearby,
the <s>indranīla</s> is described as having four great qualities.
I shall tell their shades too, just as they were stated by the ancients.
By the division into four classes, they are superior, inferior, and middling.
A blue one has the appearance of a parrot's neck, or the brilliance of a flax flower,
or it resembles the neck of a cuckoo, or has a brilliance like a peacock's neck.
Its luster is seen to be varied, like a crow's wing.
When it is free from faults, rich in qualities, and born from an excellent mine,
I shall state the value of a blue sapphire according to the estimation of the jewel.
The value that has been declared for a padmarāga possessing good qualities,
that same value has been declared by the sages for the <s>Śakranīla</s>.
One should throw a blue sapphire into the middle of milk; if it is a fine blue stone, that milk becomes blue.
It is to be known as an <s>indranīla</s> by those skilled in jewel science.
That stone which is distinguished by these qualities is beneficial to people.
The examination of the <s>Śakranīla</s> has been taught by the wise.
